Formulation
- Predisposing factors: History of chronic eczema and asthma; family history of thyroid disease and migraine.
- Precipitating factors: Recent worsening over the past few days with widespread involvement (chest, hands, arms, inside elbows) and increased itch.
- Perpetuating factors: Current OTC hydrocortisone and previous OTC antihistamine reported as ineffective; ongoing dryness and scratching with some skin cracking.
- Protective factors: Regular use of emollients (Diprobase and shower product), patient sought medical review, clinician arranged prescription and follow-up plan.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Worsening eczema/dermatitis
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce itching and skin soreness
  - Improve skin dryness and overall rash
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Reduce inflammation and pruritus, promote healing of skin lesions
  - Achieve symptomatic improvement within 2 weeks; reassess if no improvement
- Actions (Patient):
  - Continue daily emollient use (Diprobase) and shower product ("dermal") as previously used
  - Apply Betnovate topical steroid as instructed: small fingertip amount to affected areas twice daily for the next couple of weeks
  - Start oral antihistamine (fexofenadine) as prescribed (dose/route/frequency not documented)
  - Avoid excessive scratching; monitor skin for worsening, new symptoms, or signs of adverse reaction
  - Return or contact clinic/pharmacy if no improvement after 2 weeks or earlier if symptoms worsen or adverse reaction occurs
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Prescribed fexofenadine (dose/route/frequency not documented) and Betnovate topical steroid (topical, twice daily for ~2 weeks)
  - Advised amount of topical steroid (small fingertip amount to cover affected areas)
  - Sent prescription to Boots pharmacy for patient collection
  - Advised continued use of emollients and shower product
  - Advised to re-contact clinic prior to 2-week review if worsening or allergic-type reaction

Secondary Problem: Asthma (intermittent)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Not recorded

  - Not recorded

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered:
  - Explanation that eczema appears widespread and has worsened recently
  - Instruction on Betnovate topical application (use small fingertip amount; twice daily; limited duration)
  - Continue emollients (Diprobase and shower product)
  - Prescription process (sent to Boots pharmacy)
  - When to seek care: if symptoms worsen, no improvement after 2 weeks, or if signs of allergic reaction/adverse effects
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - Increased rash severity or spread, persistent/worsening itching, development of skin weeping/infection, or adverse reaction to medications (patient advised to contact clinic)
